## MPPT.dbc

| Device (Source) | Description |
|---|---|
| `Mppt` | The two MPPTs (maximum power point trackers), named Javed and Woof. Each takes power from part of the solar array and converts it to charge the battery. TODO: add the MPPT make and model, and which part of Peri's solar array each MPPT (Javed, Woof) is connected to. |
| `Telemetry` | The telemetry board, which polls the MPPTs (see Telemetry.dbc). |

<a id="mpptpolljaved-0x711"></a>

### MpptPollJaved (0x711)

Request from the telemetry board asking the Javed MPPT to send its status (message Javed). Sent every mppt_update ms (Telemetry/config.txt).

| | |
|---|---|
| From | `Telemetry` |
| CAN ID | 0x711 (1809) |
| Length | 1 bytes |
| Sent every | 1000 ms |
| InfluxDB measurement | `"Telemetry/MpptPollJaved"` |

| Signal (InfluxDB field) | Meaning | Unit | Scaling | Range | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Blank` | Not used: the request carries no data. |  | none |  |  |

Example InfluxDB query:

```
SELECT "Blank" FROM "Telemetry/MpptPollJaved" WHERE time > now() - 1h
```

<details><summary>Bit layout</summary>

```
                      Bit

         7   6   5   4   3   2   1   0
       +---+---+---+---+---+---+---+---+
 B   0 |<-----------------------------x|
 y     +---+---+---+---+---+---+---+---+
 t       +-- Blank
 e
```

</details>

<a id="javed-0x771"></a>

### Javed (0x771)

Status of the MPPT named Javed, sent in reply to each MpptPollJaved request from the telemetry board (every mppt_update ms, Telemetry/config.txt).

| | |
|---|---|
| From | `Mppt` |
| CAN ID | 0x771 (1905) |
| Length | 7 bytes |
| Sent every | 1000 ms |
| InfluxDB measurement | `"Mppt/Javed"` |

| Signal (InfluxDB field) | Meaning | Unit | Scaling | Range | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OverTemperature` | 1 if the MPPT reports that it is too hot. |  | none |  | 0 = No, 1 = Yes |
| `NoCharge` | 1 if the MPPT reports that it is not charging. TODO: add the conditions that set this flag, from the MPPT datasheet. |  | none |  | 0 = No, 1 = Yes |
| `UnderVoltage` | 1 if the MPPT reports an undervoltage. TODO: add whether this is the solar array (input) or battery (output) side, from the MPPT datasheet. |  | none |  | 0 = No, 1 = Yes |
| `BatteryVoltageLevelReached` | 1 if the battery has reached the MPPT's maximum output voltage, so the MPPT is limiting the charge. |  | none |  | 0 = No, 1 = Yes |
| `VoltageIn` | Voltage from the solar array into this MPPT (scaling from the MPPT datasheet, as previously applied in live_power.py). | V | raw x 0.15049 | 0 to 153.951 |  |
| `CurrentIn` | Current from the solar array into this MPPT (scaling from the MPPT datasheet, as previously applied in live_power.py). | A | raw x 0.00872 | 0 to 8.92056 |  |
| `VoltageOut` | Output voltage of this MPPT (battery side). TODO: add scaling and unit from the MPPT datasheet (still the raw value; check whether it is 208.79 mV per bit, as on similar MPPTs). |  | none |  |  |
| `AmbientTemperature` | Temperature inside this MPPT. TODO: add scaling and unit from the MPPT datasheet (still the raw value). |  | none |  |  |

Example InfluxDB query:

```
SELECT "OverTemperature" FROM "Mppt/Javed" WHERE time > now() - 1h
```

     0 |<-x|<-x|<-x|<-x|   |   |<------|

<a id="orion"></a>

## Orion.dbc

| Device (Source) | Description |
|---|---|
| `Orion` | Orion BMS (battery management system). It monitors every cell's voltage, the pack temperatures and the pack current, and switches the pack contactors. Its CAN messages are set up in the Orion BMS utility, so the scaling of every signal depends on the profile loaded on Peri's BMS. |

<a id="packparameters-0x700"></a>

### PackParameters (0x700)

Battery pack summary: current, voltage, state of charge and relay states.

| | |
|---|---|
| From | `Orion` |
| CAN ID | 0x700 (1792) |
| Length | 7 bytes |
| Sent every | 104 ms |
| InfluxDB measurement | `"Orion/PackParameters"` |

| Signal (InfluxDB field) | Meaning | Unit | Scaling | Range | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `PackCurrent` | Battery pack current. TODO: add the unit, scaling and sign from the Orion BMS profile loaded on Peri (Orion BMS utility); still the raw value. Orion profiles commonly use 0.1 A per bit, signed, positive = discharging, but this file decodes it as unsigned. |  | none |  |  |
| `PackInstVoltage` | Total battery pack voltage, measured right now (instantaneous). TODO: add the unit and scaling from the Orion BMS profile loaded on Peri (Orion BMS utility); still the raw value. Orion profiles commonly use 0.1 V per bit (the test capture shows 1305, which would be 130.5 V). |  | none |  |  |
| `PackSoc` | Battery state of charge: how full the battery is. TODO: add the unit and scaling from the Orion BMS profile loaded on Peri (Orion BMS utility); still the raw value. Orion profiles commonly use 0.5 % per bit (the test capture shows 159, which would be 79.5 %). |  | none |  |  |
| `RelayState` | Which of the BMS's relay and contactor outputs are on, one bit each. TODO: add the meaning of each bit, from the Orion BMS profile loaded on Peri. |  | none |  |  |

Example InfluxDB query:

```
SELECT "PackCurrent" FROM "Orion/PackParameters" WHERE time > now() - 1h
```

<a id="telemetry"></a>

## Telemetry.dbc

| Device (Source) | Description |
|---|---|
| `Telemetry` | The DUSC telemetry board (Arduino Mega 2560, see Telemetry/README.md). It adds its own GPS and status messages to the CAN bus, and polls the MPPTs. |

<a id="timeandfix-0x0f6"></a>

### TimeAndFix (0x0F6)

GPS date, time and fix status, from the telemetry board's GPS. Sent every gps_update ms (Telemetry/config.txt). The receiver uses it to set the clock for every other message.

| | |
|---|---|
| From | `Telemetry` |
| CAN ID | 0x0F6 (246) |
| Length | 8 bytes |
| Sent every | 2000 ms |
| InfluxDB measurement | `"Telemetry/TimeAndFix"` |

| Signal (InfluxDB field) | Meaning | Unit | Scaling | Range | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GpsHour` | Hour of the GPS time, UTC (0 to 23). | h | none | 0 to 23 |  |
| `GpsMinute` | Minute of the GPS time. | min | none | 0 to 59 |  |
| `GpsSeconds` | Second of the GPS time. | s | none | 0 to 59 |  |
| `GpsDay` | Day of the month of the GPS date. 0 until the GPS has obtained the time. |  | none | 0 to 31 |  |
| `GpsMonth` | Month of the GPS date (1 to 12). 0 until the GPS has obtained the time. |  | none | 0 to 12 |  |
| `GpsYear` | Year of the GPS date, last two digits only (e.g. 26 for 2026). |  | none | 0 to 99 |  |
| `GpsFix` | Whether the GPS has a position fix. |  | none | 0 to 1 | 0 = No fix, 1 = Fix |
| `GpsFixquality` | How the GPS position was obtained (NMEA fix quality). |  | none | 0 to 2 | 0 = Invalid, 1 = GPS, 2 = Differential GPS |

Example InfluxDB query:

```
SELECT "GpsHour" FROM "Telemetry/TimeAndFix" WHERE time > now() - 1h
```

<a id="systemstatusmessages-0x111"></a>

### SystemStatusMessages (0x111)

Telemetry board health. Sent every status_update ms (Telemetry/config.txt). Most bytes use the codes 0xFF good, 0xAA bad, 0xBB using defaults, 0x00 unknown (see Telemetry/README.md).

| | |
|---|---|
| From | `Telemetry` |
| CAN ID | 0x111 (273) |
| Length | 8 bytes |
| Sent every | 1000 ms |
| InfluxDB measurement | `"Telemetry/SystemStatusMessages"` |

| Signal (InfluxDB field) | Meaning | Unit | Scaling | Range | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Power` | 0xFF while the board is starting up. After that, the state of the sleep input (pin 33): 1 = car on, 0 = car off. TODO: add what the sleep input (pin 33) is wired to on Peri. |  | none |  | 255 = Starting up, 1 = Car on, 0 = Car off |
| `WritingToSd` | Whether the board is logging every message to its SD card. |  | none |  | 255 = Good, 170 = Bad, 187 = Using defaults, 0 = Unknown |
| `GpsTimeObtained` | Whether the GPS time was obtained at start-up, within time_fix ms (Telemetry/config.txt). |  | none |  | 255 = Good, 170 = Bad, 187 = Using defaults, 0 = Unknown |
| `LoadedConfig` | Whether config.txt was loaded from the SD card (0xFF loaded, 0xBB using defaults). Once the SD log file is open this is replaced by 100 + NN, where the log file is named YYMMDDNN.BIN, or by 90 if the log file could not be opened. |  | none |  | 255 = Good, 170 = Bad, 187 = Using defaults, 0 = Unknown, 90 = Log file could not be opened |
| `Flag` | State of the marker flag input (pin 22), 0 or 1, for marking a moment in the data. TODO: add what the marker flag input (pin 22) is wired to on Peri, and which state means marked. |  | none |  |  |
| `Spare1` | Spare, not used (always 0). |  | none |  |  |
| `Spare2` | Spare, not used (always 0). |  | none |  |  |
| `Spare3` | Spare, not used (always 0). |  | none |  |  |

Example InfluxDB query:

```
SELECT "Power" FROM "Telemetry/SystemStatusMessages" WHERE time > now() - 1h
```

| `DriverControls_Right` | Driver controls for the second (right) motor controller, from an earlier two-motor set-up. TODO: add whether Peri uses these; if not, remove their messages (0x41 to 0x43) from this file. |

<a id="left_status-0x101"></a>

### Left_Status (0x101)

Left motor controller status. From an earlier two-motor set-up (separate left and right controllers). Not seen in Tests/data/NRT.BIN. TODO: add whether Peri uses this message; if not, remove it from this file.

| | |
|---|---|
| From | `Tritium` |
| CAN ID | 0x101 (257) |
| Length | 8 bytes |
| Sent every | not known |
| InfluxDB measurement | `"Tritium/Left_Status"` |

| Signal (InfluxDB field) | Meaning | Unit | Scaling | Range | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `LimitFlagBridgePWM` | 1 = output is being limited by the bridge PWM. |  | none |  |  |
| `LimitFlagMotorCurrent` | 1 = output is being limited by the motor current limit. |  | none |  |  |
| `LimitFlagVelocity` | 1 = output is being limited by the velocity limit. |  | none |  |  |
| `LimitFlagBusCurrent` | 1 = output is being limited by the bus current limit. |  | none |  |  |
| `LimitFlagBusVoltageUpperLimit` | 1 = output is being limited by the bus voltage upper limit. |  | none |  |  |
| `LimitFlagBusVoltageLowerLimit` | 1 = output is being limited by the bus voltage lower limit. |  | none |  |  |
| `LimitFlagHeatsinkTemperature` | 1 = output is being limited by the heatsink temperature. |  | none |  |  |
| `ErrorFlagHWOvercurrent` | 1 = hardware over current error. |  | none |  |  |
| `ErrorFlagSWOvercurrent` | 1 = software over current error. |  | none |  |  |
| `ErrorFlagDCBusOvervoltage` | 1 = DC bus over voltage error. |  | none |  |  |
| `ErrorFlagMotorPositionHallSequence` | 1 = bad motor position hall sequence error. |  | none |  |  |
| `ErrorFlagWatchdog` | 1 = the watchdog caused the last reset. |  | none |  |  |
| `ErrorFlagConfigRead` | 1 = config read error (some settings may have been reset to defaults). |  | none |  |  |
| `ErrorFlag15VUndervoltage` | 1 = a 15 V rail under voltage lock out occurred. |  | none |  |  |
| `ActiveMotor` | Index of the motor profile currently in use. |  | none |  |  |

Example InfluxDB query:

```
SELECT "LimitFlagBridgePWM" FROM "Tritium/Left_Status" WHERE time > now() - 1h
```

<a id="statusinformation-0x601"></a>

### StatusInformation (0x601)

Motor controller status: which limits are active, errors, and CAN error counts.

| From | `Tritium` |

| Signal (InfluxDB field) | Meaning | Unit | Scaling | Range | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `LimitFlags` | Which limit is currently restricting the controller's output, one bit each (bit 0 bridge PWM, bit 1 motor current, bit 2 velocity, bit 3 bus current, bit 4 bus voltage upper limit, bit 5 bus voltage lower limit, bit 6 heatsink temperature). |  | none |  |  |
| `ErrorFlags` | Error flags, one bit each (bit 0 hardware over current, bit 1 software over current, bit 2 DC bus over voltage, bit 3 bad motor position hall sequence, bit 4 watchdog caused the last reset, bit 5 config read error, bit 6 15 V rail under voltage lock out). 0 = no errors. TODO: add the remaining bits from the WaveSculptor22 user manual. |  | none |  |  |
| `ActiveMotor` | Index of the motor profile currently in use. |  | none |  |  |
| `TransmitErrorCount` | Number of CAN transmit errors counted by the controller. |  | none |  |  |
| `ReceiveErrorCount` | Number of CAN receive errors counted by the controller. |  | none |  |  |

SELECT "LimitFlags" FROM "Tritium/StatusInformation" WHERE time > now() - 1h
